title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: Which Declaration Is Judged for Lateness and Its Signing Date
content:
## Clause

Lateness on a Dangerous Goods Acceptance file is judged on one declaration only: the acceptance's initial declaration in its signed form. If the declaration file holds more than one signed initial declaration, the one registered last is judged. An initial declaration that is unsigned, sent back for correction or withdrawn is never the one judged, and an acceptance with no signed initial declaration at all owes no late declaration fee.

Amendment declarations are outside this test altogether. They answer to the amendment deadline instead and never give rise to a late declaration fee.

## The signing date

The declaration file keeps one date for a signature and one only: the moment at which the signed submission was registered. That registration moment therefore stands as the shipper's signing date for the judged declaration, and its lead time runs from it.

## Input, judgement, output

| Declaration file of the acceptance | Declaration judged | Signing date used |
|---|---|---|
| one signed initial declaration | that declaration | its registration date |
| two signed initial declarations | the one registered later | its registration date |
| one initial declaration awaiting signature, no signed one | none — no late fee | — |
| a signed initial declaration and a signed amendment | the initial declaration | the initial declaration's registration date |

## Point of judgement

**The shipper says it signed on paper two days earlier than the registration shows.** The file's registration moment is the only signing date the line uses.
